A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SurvDiff by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-fidelity, downstream survival, Kaplan-Meier, and reduced-sample experiments on AIDS, GBSG2, and METABRIC.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the same datasets, including new temporal-fidelity, private-training, and ablation results. Some explicitly attributed Ashhad results are borrowed, but extensive original results remain.

M1.justification: The central joint diffusion model, survival head, and calibrated Cox-loss weighting remain. Table 4 changes the listed MLP depths from 2 to 3 and survival-MLP depth from 1 to 2. Appendix I adds an optional DP-SGD variant using per-sample gradient clipping and Gaussian noise.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIDS, GBSG2, and METABRIC with the same populations and survival endpoints. The additions analyze retained data or change training and evaluation procedures; they introduce no new dataset, medical domain, or underlying prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 adds Ashhad to Tables 2–3, real-data-trained survival models as a reference in Table 3, and DP-GAN in the new private-training comparison. Some Ashhad entries are explicitly taken from its papers. The original five generative baselines remain, and comparative Kaplan-Meier plots also expand baseline participation.

E3.justification: Table 4 revises SurvDiff's epochs from 4000 to 1200, warm-up from 1500 to 150, maximum noise from 80 to 20, and learning rate from 0.002 to 0.001. v2 adds Shape and ETD metrics, ablation controls, parameter sweeps, and private evaluation at epsilon 8 and delta 10^-5. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix J newly isolates duration-dependent weighting with a w=1 ablation and tests four decay-parameter values. Appendices C–E add event-time-conditioned covariate comparisons, marginal distributions, and separate censored/uncensored temporal analyses. The reduced-sample study is retained, while SurvDiff-only seed plots are replaced by comparative covariate/Kaplan-Meier panels.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across ten seeds for their principal experiments. The new private-training and ablation tables follow that practice. No increased replication count, significance testing, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially revise existing results: SurvDiff's AIDS C-index changes from 0.6826 to 0.7017, while its METABRIC Brier score changes from 0.1924 to 0.2120. Kaplan-Meier results also change, and Shape, ETD, privacy, and ablation results are added. These are revised results under changed reported settings, not controlled performance gains. The downsampling table is numerically retained.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 8 corrects the Cox-loss denominator from exp(r_i) in v1 Equation 10 to exp(r_j) inside the risk-set sum. v2 also formally defines ETD and differential privacy and gives a clipped-gradient update. The existing diffusion mathematics is substantially retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the novelty claim from the first diffusion model for synthetic survival data to the first end-to-end diffusion model. The introduction's three contributions and the conclusion's central joint-generation and fidelity claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new temporal analyses as preserving patient composition across event horizons and avoiding concentration at frequent event times. Appendix J attributes modest benefits to duration weighting and argues for parameter robustness; Appendix I adds an interpretation of robustness under private training. The clinical rationale and RMST cancellation caveat are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, Ashhad hyperparameters, SynthCity implementation provenance, and detailed metric-computation instructions in Appendix B.1. These specify synthetic sample counts, preprocessing, histogram construction and smoothing, scaling, and the Sinkhorn solver. It also adds dropout/weight-decay disclosures and privacy-training information while revising existing hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 and Table 1 newly acknowledge the Ashhad–Henao framework alongside SurvivalGAN and explain their staged generation relative to SurvDiff's end-to-end design. TabDDPM, SynthCity, and differential-privacy references are also added. Most previous research positioning remains; the swapped TabDiff citation suffix is merely bibliographic.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and explanatory passages, organizes fidelity around four categories, promotes Results to a separate section, and expands and renames appendices. Most existing method and discussion prose remains close to v1, so the substantial scientific additions do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: Experimental plots are extensively redrawn with revised colors, annotations, and panel arrangements. The main METABRIC t-SNE display moves to the appendix, while temporal distributions enter the main text. New marginal and temporal plots, comparative Kaplan-Meier panels, expanded Tables 2–3, and new ETD, privacy, and ablation tables substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central survival-generation claim through direct weighting ablations and event-time-conditioned fidelity evidence that v1 lacked. The additional Ashhad comparison, corrected Cox equation, and explicit metric-computation details also improve assessment and reproducibility. ETD's inconsistent equal-width/equal-mass bin descriptions and incomplete privacy-accounting details limit parts of the new material, but the evidence supporting evaluation of the core method is substantially stronger overall.
